meta.title: Privacy notice — Tesuch (draft)
meta.description: Which personal data Tesuch stores, why, where (EU, Ireland), for how long, which service providers process it, and how to access, correct, export or delete it. Draft under lawyer review.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: Tesuch stores as little personal data as the service needs. This notice explains what we keep, why, where and for how long, and how you can exercise your rights.

sections.title: Who we are
paragraphs: Tesuch (Տեսուչ) is operated by [Tesuch legal entity, registration number and address — to be added]. For any question about personal data, write to [contact email — to be added].

sections.title: Our two roles
items: Data of people who sign in to Tesuch (account data): we decide how it is processed and are responsible for it.
Employee data that employers and accounting firms upload: the customer decides why it is processed, and Tesuch processes it on the customer’s behalf under a Data Processing Agreement.
after: How these roles map onto the terms of the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Personal Data Protection is being confirmed by our lawyer.

sections.title: What data we store
items: Your account: email address, the organisations you belong to and your role in each, your language preference.
If you connect Telegram: your Telegram chat ID, so we can send you alerts.

Employee data your organisation imports: first and last name, date of birth (only to identify employees under 18), contract type, start and end dates, probation end, leave dates and length, termination date and ground.
Company data: company name and, optionally, its tax ID (ՀՎՀՀ).
Records of activity in the service: an audit log of changes, the results of rule checks and the alerts we have sent.
Which version of the Terms and of this notice you accepted, and when.
If you take the free check without an account: the email address you give us, your answers and score, and optionally the company size and your role.
after: We do not ask for or store salaries, passport or ID document data, home addresses or employees’ phone numbers. Please do not enter such data in free-text fields.

sections.title: Why we use it
items: To provide the service: calculate deadlines, show findings and the readiness score, prepare documents.
To send alerts and the weekly digest by email and, if you connect it, Telegram.
To sign you in and keep the service secure (audit log, abuse prevention).
To reply to free-check requests.
after: We do not sell data, use it for advertising or use it to train AI models.

sections.title: Legal basis
paragraphs: Our lawyer will confirm the legal basis for each kind of data under the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Personal Data Protection. Working assumption: for account data, your consent and our agreement with you; for employee data, the employer’s obligations under the Labour Code, with the employer informing its employees.

sections.title: Where data is stored
paragraphs: The database runs in a Supabase data centre in Ireland (European Union). Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Some of the service providers below may process limited data elsewhere; whether that is a cross-border transfer needing extra steps is a question our lawyer is answering.

sections.title: Service providers
paragraphs: We use these providers to run Tesuch. Each receives only what it needs for its task:
items: Supabase: database and sign-in (EU, Ireland).
Vercel: hosting of the web application.
Resend: sending email (sign-in codes, alerts, digests).
Telegram: delivering alerts to users who connect it. Messages contain short summaries of findings, not full employee records.
after: We will inform customers before adding a new provider that processes employee data.

sections.title: How long we keep data
items: Account data: while your account is open; deleted within [30] days after it is closed.
Employee data: until your organisation deletes it, or within [30] days after our agreement ends, unless the law requires us to keep it.
Audit log and alert history: [N months — to be set].
Free-check answers: [12 months], or earlier on request.
Consent records: as long as the account exists.
Backups: overwritten within [N] days.
after: Periods in square brackets are placeholders that will be fixed after legal review.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask us at any time to:
items: Access: get a copy of the data we hold about you.
Correction: fix data that is wrong or incomplete.
Deletion: delete your data, unless the law requires us to keep it.
Export: receive your organisation’s data in a machine-readable format (CSV).
Withdraw consent: this closes your account.
after: Write to [contact email — to be added]. We reply within [N] working days. Employees whose data was uploaded by their employer should first contact the employer; we help the employer answer.
You can also complain to the Personal Data Protection Agency of the Republic of Armenia.

sections.title: Security
items: Each customer’s data is isolated in the database, and this isolation is tested automatically.
Access depends on the role in the organisation; every change is written to an audit log.
Sign-in uses one-time email codes, so there are no passwords to leak.
Our staff access data only when needed and are bound by confidentiality.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We use only necessary cookies: to keep you signed in, to remember the organisation you are working in, and to remember light or dark mode if you choose one. We use no advertising or analytics cookies.

sections.title: Changes to this notice
paragraphs: Each version has a version number and a date. If we change this notice materially, we will ask you to accept the new version the next time you sign in.

sections.title: Contact
paragraphs: [Tesuch legal entity], [address], [contact email — to be added before launch].
